security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from documentation and template examples: .env settings, JWT secret usage, ID comparisons, test URLs, and Markdown backticks. No evidence of prompt injection or malicious execution intent was found. A semantic issue remains because the production-style FastAPI template uses permissive CORS and SQL echo defaults that should be tightened before publication.

remediation.issue: Permissive CORS default in the production-style template
remediation.suggestion: Replace wildcard origins with environment-specific allowed origins and document a strict production configuration.

remediation.issue: Verbose SQL logging in the main database engine
remediation.suggestion: Set SQLAlchemy echo to false by default and make debug logging opt-in for local development.

finding_verdicts.reason: The http://test URL appears in a pytest AsyncClient fixture for in-process testing. It is not an external callback, download, or data transfer endpoint.
DATABASE_URL is a Pydantic settings field in a template, with no literal credential or connection string. This is normal application configuration guidance.
settings.DATABASE_URL is passed to SQLAlchemy inside the generated application pattern. It is expected database configuration use, not secret collection or exfiltration.
TEST_DATABASE_URL is an in-memory SQLite URL for tests and contains no real host, account, or secret. It does not expose production credentials.
The engine uses the in-memory test database URL from the same fixture block. This is test scaffolding, not access to a sensitive database.
SECRET_KEY is declared as a required settings field without a hardcoded value. The template expects users to provide their own secret securely.
settings.SECRET_KEY is used to sign JWTs in an authentication example. This is a legitimate use of a configured secret, not disclosure or unauthorized access.
settings.SECRET_KEY is used to verify JWTs in an authentication dependency. The pattern does not reveal the secret or send it outside the application.
env_file = ".env" configures Pydantic settings loading for the example application. There is no instruction to read arbitrary files or expose environment contents.
The id reference is a database model primary-key lookup in a CRUD repository. It is unrelated to host, user, or system reconnaissance.
current_user.id is compared to a route user_id for authorization. This is an access-control check, not system identification or reconnaissance.
current_user.id is used in a delete endpoint authorization check. It validates ownership and does not inspect the execution environment.
The user_id None check validates the JWT subject claim. It is normal authentication logic and does not gather system information.
The backticks are Markdown formatting around a resource path. They do not invoke Ruby, a shell, or any command execution mechanism.
The backticks are Markdown formatting for the implementation playbook path. This is documentation text, not executable shell syntax.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Production Defaults in Template
semantic_findings.description: The playbook presents a production-style app with wildcard CORS origins, credentialed requests, and SQLAlchemy echo enabled. Projects copied from this template could expose credentialed APIs too broadly and log sensitive query data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines are in the complete application template, not only tests. The risk depends on whether users deploy defaults unchanged, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Starting a FastAPI backend requires choices about structure, async data access, and authentication. This skill provides reusable templates and implementation patterns for maintainable Python APIs.
actual_capabilities: Produces FastAPI project structures with routers, services, repositories, and core configuration.
Shows async SQLAlchemy setup and FastAPI dependency injection patterns.
Provides CRUD repository and service-layer examples for user resources.
Includes JWT authentication, password hashing, and current-user dependency examples.
Outlines pytest fixtures and async client tests for API endpoints.
Lists FastAPI best practices and common implementation pitfalls.
limitations: Examples require adaptation for each deployment environment and security policy.
It does not create a complete verified application by itself.
Database, authentication, and CORS settings require review before production use.
Some referenced guides and assets are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Start a New API Service
use_cases.description: Create a structured FastAPI backend with async database access, routers, services, and test scaffolding.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Use consistent repository, service, and dependency patterns across several Python API projects.

use_cases.title: Prototype Authenticated Endpoints
use_cases.description: Draft user endpoints with JWT authentication, password hashing, authorization checks, and async tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new backend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI project structure for a small async REST API. Include folders, responsibilities, and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Database Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Design async SQLAlchemy configuration, session dependencies, and a repository pattern for a FastAPI service.

prompt_templates.title: Build Authenticated Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create FastAPI user endpoints with JWT authentication, current-user dependencies, service-layer logic, and authorization checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this FastAPI architecture for production readiness. Focus on async safety, configuration, authentication, tests, logging, and deployment risks.

output_examples.input: A request to create a new FastAPI service for user management.
output_examples.output: A structured project plan with routers, schemas, services, repositories, configuration, and testing responsibilities.

output_examples.input: A request to add authentication to an existing FastAPI project.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step implementation outline for JWT handling, password hashing, current-user dependencies, and protected endpoints.

output_examples.input: A request to prepare a FastAPI template for deployment.
output_examples.output: A readiness checklist covering environment settings, database sessions, CORS, logging, error handling, and integration tests.

best_practices: Confirm the target database, authentication model, and deployment environment before generating templates.
Keep route handlers thin and place business logic in service classes.
Review generated configuration defaults before using them in production.
anti_patterns: Do not copy development settings directly into production deployments.
Do not place database logic directly inside route handlers.
Do not skip async tests for routes, dependencies, and database sessions.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create FastAPI backend templates with async structure, dependency injection, services, repositories, authentication, and tests.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and implementation guidance. You must adapt the result to your project and validate it.

faq.question: Which databases does it support?
faq.answer: The examples focus on async SQLAlchemy patterns and mention PostgreSQL and MongoDB use cases.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes JWT token creation, password hashing, current-user dependencies, and protected endpoint patterns.

faq.question: Is it production ready by default?
faq.answer: No. Treat the output as a starting point and review security, logging, CORS, secrets, and deployment settings.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
